protocols.title: Quantifier and decision-contract audit
protocols.method: Checks universal quantifiers, both SAT/UNSAT branches, termination, recovery, and whether the exact conclusion follows from the stated premises.
protocols.failure_signal: A missing branch, vacuous quantifier, or conclusion not implied by the stated contract.

protocols.title: Hidden-oracle and circularity audit
protocols.method: Searches for solve-and-encode behavior, semantic canonization, nonuniform advice, or a subroutine that already decides the target problem.
protocols.failure_signal: The construction can decide the target problem before emitting the claimed representation.

protocols.title: Uniformity and explicitness audit
protocols.method: Requires one uniform polynomial-time constructor, explicit family, fixed proof system, or fixed algorithm rather than an existential placeholder.
protocols.failure_signal: The statement lacks a fixed uniform constructor, explicit family, or exact proof-system syntax.

protocols.title: Resource and bit-complexity audit
protocols.method: Charges time, symbols, degree, coefficient bit length, precision, memory, expanded representation, and certificate size.
protocols.failure_signal: A hidden superpolynomial resource appears in time, size, degree, precision, or bit length.

protocols.title: Soundness, completeness, and witness audit
protocols.method: Checks both directions of correctness and exact extraction of a satisfying assignment or refutation certificate.
protocols.failure_signal: One correctness direction or witness/refutation extraction is missing.

protocols.title: Model-transfer audit
protocols.method: Requires every claimed simulation or lower-bound transfer to preserve the exact syntax, field, degree, size, and coefficient measures.
protocols.failure_signal: The transfer changes field, syntax, proof shape, degree, size, or coefficient measure.

protocols.title: Auxiliary-variable and projection audit
protocols.method: Separates functional definitions from existential fibers and tests whether forgetting auxiliaries destroys the proposed invariant.
protocols.failure_signal: Auxiliary-variable forgetting or nonfunctional fibers erase the claimed invariant.

protocols.title: Explicit counterfamily and restriction audit
protocols.method: Attacks the statement with expanders, Tseitin, pigeonhole, mixed XOR/non-affine families, random restrictions, and residual-width preservation.
protocols.failure_signal: An explicit hard family or large restriction survives all permitted preprocessing.

protocols.title: Complexity-barrier scope audit
protocols.method: Checks relativization, natural-proofs, algebrization, proof-complexity barriers, and whether cited results cover only restricted fragments.
protocols.failure_signal: The argument crosses a known barrier or extrapolates from a restricted fragment.

protocols.title: Parent-dependency audit
protocols.method: Propagates unresolved obligations and terminal failures through derived_from links without treating parent survival as evidence.
protocols.failure_signal: The child depends on an unresolved or terminal parent obligation without repairing it.

protocols.title: Mutual-incompatibility audit
protocols.method: Registers pairs that cannot both be true and forbids interpreting simultaneous OPEN status as joint plausibility.
protocols.failure_signal: Two live statements are logically incompatible, so at least one must eventually fail.

protocols.title: Independent-reproduction audit
protocols.method: Requires committed artifacts, deterministic inputs, exact arithmetic where claimed, and a verifier independent of the generator.
protocols.failure_signal: The result cannot be reproduced from committed deterministic artifacts and exact checks.

claim_boundary: These are reusable audit protocols, not automated theorem provers. A nonterminal result records only the outcome of the stated audit.
